column1: # analyte_digit_curated.tsv — manual overlay for the auto-mined alias
# table. The build (`mirobody indicator analyte-digit`) never touches
# this file; entries here survive every refresh.
# Format (tab-separated, no header):
#   <canonical_name>  <digit>  <family>  [optional_note]
# - canonical_name : lowercase, regex-matched verbatim against LOINC
#                    display names (case-insensitive, \b-anchored)
# - digit          : the numeric subtype the canonical name implicitly
#                    represents (B1 → 1, K2 → 2, IGF-2 → 2)
# - family         : single-letter family tag (B / K / D / A / IGF /
#                    IGFBP) — informational, helps reviewers group rows
# Add an entry when:
#   1. LOINC's `RELATEDNAMES2` and SNOMED CT synonyms both omit the
#      numeric-shortname alias (LOINC sometimes uses historical names
#      that don't map cleanly: `Vit H` for Biotin = B7, `Vit M` for
#      Folate = B9).
#   2. The subtype has no LOINC code at all but you want queries to
#      null-out rather than fall to a cosine-close sibling (Menaquinone
#      = K2 — LOINC has K1 Phytonadione and K3 Menadione only).
#   3. A colloquial chemical name appears in queries that the auto
#      sources don't list.
# folate / folic acid → 9 (B9): LOINC's `RELATEDNAMES2` for Folate
# lists `Vit M; Vitamin M` (deprecated nomenclature) but not `Vit B9`.
# SNOMED has no `B9` synonym for Folate either.
folate
folic acid
pteroylglutamate
pteroylglutamic acid
# menaquinone / menatetrenone → 2 (K2): LOINC has no measurement code
# for K2 — only K1 (Phytonadione) and K3 (Menadione). Including K2
# here means a query `Vitamin K2` against the K1 Phytonadione cosine
# top-1 fails the digit check (the augmented Phytonadione row carries
# digit 1, not 2) and nulls correctly.
menaquinone
menatetrenone
# nicotinic acid / nicotinamide → 3 (B3): SNOMED maps these as
# separate substance concepts from Niacin but doesn't include the
# `Vit B3` synonym on them. LOINC mining picks them up via Niacin's
# RELATEDNAMES2 but only under the Niacin canonical. Listing them
# here covers LOINC rows whose display name uses the alternate
# chemical form (e.g., specialty assays).
nicotinic acid
nicotinamide
# pantothenic acid → 5 (B5): SNOMED has it, but only the FSN form;
# LOINC uses `Pantothenate` (the carboxylate form) for the assay
# concept. Listed here so LOINC rows naming the acid form also pick
# up the alias.
pantothenic acid
# methylcobalamin / aquacobalamin → 12 (B12): LOINC mining captures
# Hydroxocobalamin via RELATEDNAMES2 but methylcobalamin's LOINC
# rows (when present) sometimes lack the `Vit B12` related-name.
# Cobalamins (the LOINC COMPONENT for B12) covers most queries, but
# specialty assays for the active methyl form benefit from this
# explicit alias.
methylcobalamin
aquacobalamin
# phylloquinone → 1 (K1): synonym for Phytonadione. LOINC's
# `RELATEDNAMES2` for Phytonadione lists it, so it's auto-picked, but
# kept here as documentation in case a future LOINC release re-axes
# the family.
phylloquinone
# cv2 → 5 (CRMP-5): paraneoplastic-antibody analyte. LOINC names the
# row `CV2 IgG Ab` (the antigen historical name) but clinical queries
# use the modern protein name `CRMP-5` / `Collapsin response mediator
# protein 5`. Without this alias the cosine-correct CV2 row carries
# only the auto-extracted digit 2 (from `CV2`), so a query `CRMP-5`
# (q_digit=5) hits the digit-aware null-out guard and returns empty.
# Mapping CV2 → 5 lets the CV2 row's augmented digits cover both
# views: 2 (the historical CV2 antigen number) and 5 (the CRMP family
# member number). Family tag `CRMP` is informational.
cv2
